desk.headline: Revenue up 12% to a record $114.5bn, beat; holiday-quarter sales outlook above estimates but margins squeezed by memory costs
results: Record September quarter: sales rose 12% to $114.5bn and diluted EPS rose 14% to $2.10 (5c of that came from tariff refunds).
iPhone sales grew 17% to $57.6bn and Mac 24% to $10.8bn; iPad fell to $6.2bn and Wearables, Home and Accessories fell to $8.3bn.
Services hit an all-time high of $31.6bn, up 10%; Greater China sales rose 21% to $17.5bn.
Full fiscal 2026 revenue was a record $478.8bn, up 15%, with net income of $132.2bn.
The quarter produced $28bn of operating cash flow and $28bn went back to shareholders; quarterly dividend of $0.27 declared.

guidance.summary: The press release gives no outlook. On the call, as reported, Apple guided December-quarter sales up 7–10% (its biggest December quarter yet) but gross margin of only 45–46% as memory chip costs climb.

points: Memory chips are the main reason margins are falling; CEO John Ternus called memory pricing "unprecedented" and expects it to keep rising after December.
Price increases on iPad and Mac (June) and iPhone (September) only partly offset the higher costs.
Demand for the new foldable iPhone Duo is ahead of supply, and Apple could not say when it will catch up.
Memory shortages are expected to limit Mac and iPad supply this quarter; the CFO credited new MacBooks for the Mac beat.
First results call under new CEO Ternus; the new Siri AI adds some cost.
call.source: Call coverage: StockAnalysis.com, 3 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: How far memory costs push gross margin below 46%, and whether further price rises follow.
iPhone Duo supply catching up with demand over the holiday quarter.
Services growth slowing to 8–9% versus double digits before.

sources.title: Apple's Q4 revenue grows 12% to $114.5B, but memory costs will squeeze holiday-quarter margins — StockAnalysis.com, 3 Nov 2026
